nodes.label: Patient presented with new-onset dizziness while sitting and episodes of near-syncope without loss of consciousness

A man in his 70s with history of orthotopic heart transplant (biatrial surgical technique), grade 1 cardiac allograft vasculopathy, toxic multinodular goiter status post-thyroidectomy, and tremors treated with propranolol
Two weeks prior, his cardiologist measured low blood pressure and stopped amlodipine treatment, after which symptoms improved
At presentation, physical examination showed normotension and unremarkable cardiac examination
Zio monitor recorded a 4.5-second ventricular pause with junctional escape and dual sinus node dissociation activity
Transplant-related bradyarrhythmia is the cause of dizziness and near-syncope
Orthostatic blood pressure measurements were not obtained
Detailed medication records for amlodipine and propranolol were not available for review
No biopsy, angiography, symptom diary, or laboratory data were available for diagnostic review
Propranolol is aggravating the transplant-related bradyarrhythmia
Cardiac allograft vasculopathy contributes to the bradyarrhythmia via conduction system ischemia
Transplant-related bradyarrhythmia causing dizziness and near-syncope
Propranolol-aggravated bradyarrhythmia causing dizziness and near-syncope
Cardiac allograft vasculopathy-related bradyarrhythmia causing dizziness and near-syncope
Sinus node dysfunction is the specific transplant-related bradyarrhythmia causing dizziness and near-syncope
The patient's dizziness and near-syncope are caused by transplant-related bradyarrhythmia
